motions.item_title: Committee of the Whole Consent Report
motions.text: That the June 23, 2026 Committee of the Whole Consent Report, identified below, be adopted:
motions.text_html: 1. That the June 23, 2026 Committee of the Whole Consent Report, identified below, be adopted:

motions.text: That Aird & Berlis LLP be appointed as the City of Guelph’s Closed Meeting Investigator. That the Mayor and City Clerk be authorized to execute an agreement to contract the services of Aird & Berlis LLP as the City of Guelph’s Closed Meeting Investigator. That By-law Number (2026) – 21249, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-250, dated June 2, 2026, be brought forward for approval. That the City Clerk be directed to review the Closed Meeting Protocol, the Procedure By-law, any related policies/procedures, and best practices in the management of municipal closed meetings to identify opportunities to increase transparency and reporting, as part of the 2027 Governance Review.
motions.text_html:
1. That Aird & Berlis LLP be appointed as the City of Guelph’s Closed Meeting Investigator.
  2. That the Mayor and City Clerk be authorized to execute an agreement to contract the services of Aird & Berlis LLP as the City of Guelph’s Closed Meeting Investigator.
  3. That By-law Number (2026) – 21249, included as Attachment-1 to report 2026-250, dated June 2, 2026, be brought forward for approval.
  4. That the City Clerk be directed to review the Closed Meeting Protocol, the Procedure By-law, any related policies/procedures, and best practices in the management of municipal closed meetings to identify opportunities to increase transparency and reporting, as part of the 2027 Governance Review.

motions.item_title: Recommendation Report - New Fee Structure for Building Permit Applications - 2026-251
motions.text: That the Recommendation Report - New Fee Structure for Building Permit Applications be received. That the amendment to Schedule “A” of the Building By-law (2015) – 19985, as shown in Attachment-2, be approved. That the amendment to Tables 5 and 79 of the User Fees By-law (2025) - 21164, as shown in Attachment-3, be approved. That Council approve adjusting the Building Services OBC Stabilization Reserve Fund target to be within the range of 100 to 300 per cent of prior year budget operating expenditures and direct staff to update the General Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy. That Council approve the recommended automatic fee indexing methodology for 2028 and subsequent years, as described in the Recommendation Report - New Fee Structure for Building Permit Applications. That Council direct staff to consider the advantages and disadvantages of implementing the proposed new administrative fees as set out in Section 5 of the BMA report and bring any further recommendations to Council for approval as part of the 2027 budget confirmation.
motions.text_html:
1. That the Recommendation Report - New Fee Structure for Building Permit Applications be received.
  2. That the amendment to Schedule “A” of the Building By-law (2015) – 19985, as shown in Attachment-2, be approved.
  3. That the amendment to Tables 5 and 79 of the User Fees By-law (2025) - 21164, as shown in Attachment-3, be approved.
  4. That Council approve adjusting the Building Services OBC Stabilization Reserve Fund target to be within the range of 100 to 300 per cent of prior year budget operating expenditures and direct staff to update the General Reserve and Reserve Fund Policy.
  5. That Council approve the recommended automatic fee indexing methodology for 2028 and subsequent years, as described in the Recommendation Report - New Fee Structure for Building Permit Applications.
  6. That Council direct staff to consider the advantages and disadvantages of implementing the proposed new administrative fees as set out in Section 5 of the BMA report and bring any further recommendations to Council for approval as part of the 2027 budget confirmation.

motions.item_title: Usage of City Hall as an Overnight Warming and Cooling Centre - 2026-118
motions.text: That Guelph City Council respectfully requests that The County of Wellington, as the area Social Services Manager, share their review of service and entry processes for overnight shelter admittance for individuals where barriers and restrictions exist, ensuring alternative options are available, accessible and offered as a due course of process and a 24/7phone line is available for residents to call for immediate help in case of need for extreme weather events or for those unable to physically attend available shelters due to special circumstance barriers. And, while respecting privacy laws, consider data collection for annual review by the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee that includes general reasons for refusal, restrictions, or other barriers to help inform ongoing adjustments and opportunities to improve the overnight shelter system. And, that if any changes are considered, that these be implemented prior to the upcoming 2026-2027 Winter Response Program commencing.
motions.text_html:
1. That Guelph City Council respectfully requests that The County of Wellington, as the area Social Services Manager, share their review of service and entry processes for overnight shelter admittance for individuals where barriers and restrictions exist, ensuring alternative options are available, accessible and offered as a due course of process and a 24/7phone line is available for residents to call for immediate help in case of need for extreme weather events or for those unable to physically attend available shelters due to special circumstance barriers.
  2. And, while respecting privacy laws, consider data collection for annual review by the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee that includes general reasons for refusal, restrictions, or other barriers to help inform ongoing adjustments and opportunities to improve the overnight shelter system.
  3. And, that if any changes are considered, that these be implemented prior to the upcoming 2026-2027 Winter Response Program commencing.

motions.name: Main Motion
motions.text: That Council requests that the DGBA works with City staff to determine operationally feasible parking mitigation opportunities to support customers of downtown businesses during construction activities on Wyndham Street, above and beyond the existing parking mitigation already in place; and that the cost of up to $25,000 be paid from the DTIRP construction mitigation budget while council respectfully requests matching funds of $25,000 (for a total of $50,000 towards mitigation) from the DGBA. And that Council acknowledge that increasing parking mitigation funding means that other construction mitigation actions will not be delivered unless the construction mitigation budget is topped up through the 2027 confirmation budget process. And that Council requests that the DGBA provide an update to Council on their own mitigation efforts related to downtown construction, and outline a plan for how they are contributing funds to support these efforts. That Council respectfully request that the incoming Mayor consider continued investment in similar measures for inclusion in the 2027 confirmation budget.
motions.text_html:
1.   2. And that Council acknowledge that increasing parking mitigation funding means that other construction mitigation actions will not be delivered unless the construction mitigation budget is topped up through the 2027 confirmation budget process.
  3. And that Council requests that the DGBA provide an update to Council on their own mitigation efforts related to downtown construction, and outline a plan for how they are contributing funds to support these efforts.
  4. That Council respectfully request that the incoming Mayor consider continued investment in similar measures for inclusion in the 2027 confirmation budget.
